main_result.result: Implemented a concrete whole-file CAS + append + file fsync + parent-directory fsync on creation + full readback writer. Exact expected-before+frame already present is treated as an uncertain-ack idempotent retry and is fsynced/read back without duplicate append; any other current bytes fail closed.
main_result.ack_boundary_stress: Crash injection after append-before-fsync, after fsync-before-readback and after readback-before-return returned no capability in the failed call; exact retry then succeeded and yielded a usable capability. For a 358-byte ADMIT frame, all 357 nonempty partial cuts were rejected before repair, and all 358 cut cases succeeded after recovery/truncation to the independently verified prior prefix. Exact retry produced no duplicate frame and deterministic capability identity was preserved in the harness.

measurement_validity_rules: Uncertain acknowledgement is not failure-to-persist and not success-to-launch. The only safe retry states are the exact prior durable prefix or the exact prior prefix plus the intended frame.
A nonempty torn frame must fail the writer CAS and be repaired by the journal layer to a verified valid prefix before retry; the writer must not guess the scientific recovery boundary.
An exact frame found after uncertain acknowledgement may be fsynced and read back again and then acknowledged without appending a duplicate event.
No launch capability can be returned on any injected crash path because capability delivery occurs only after the writer returns exact durable readback.
The in-process POSIX crash harness validates control flow and idempotence, not real power-loss persistence probabilities or dishonest storage-controller fsync acknowledgements.
Whole-file CAS is not cross-process mutual exclusion. If multiple launch processes are possible, add fencing/locking before treating this writer as the sole durable writer.
frontier: Byte-execute the concrete writer plus launch gate against the exact production durable adapter/V3/K-guard sibling files in a repository-local runtime.

Determine whether the actual evaluation launcher can have multiple OS processes. If yes, add a writer lease/fencing token or OS-level lock and stress stale-writer recovery; if no, record the single-process invariant explicitly.
Move capability checking to the score-generation launch boundary itself so an unauthorized job cannot consume compute or reveal a score before SLOT persistence.
Use the same writer acknowledgement discipline for CLOSE and only expose the numerical reporting snapshot after durable CLOSE readback; crash-inject residual-alpha fresh allocation at that boundary.
Define a non-retroactive legacy-journal migration path that never issues launch authority for rows lacking enriched pre-score ADMIT metadata.
exact_next_action: Implement a score-launch wrapper that requires a valid LaunchCapability before invoking any score-producing callable, binds the callable request to block_id/slot_id and the capability's exact admitted plan, and returns an opaque score result that can only be persisted through prepare_slot_authorized; stress wrong/stale/tampered capabilities and crash/retry so unauthorized work cannot become scientific evidence.
